company_description: Small-to-mid SaaS company building a conversational support assistant for B2B clients. Inbound from self-serve signup (trial credits used), early discovery to validate hosted API fit.
notes: 2026-03-09: First intro call (30m) w/ Diego (AE) + Maya (SE) + Founder (A. Gill). Good energy, demo of current prototype.
Source: inbound self-serve — used free credits, ran 1k tokens of chat + embeddings, saw jitter in responses at higher load.

Primary ask: decide which model family to standardize on for hosted API. Candidate families discussed: Llama variants (13B+), Mistral (7B/8B mixes), Qwen (7B/14B) — importance: cost vs quality and multilingual (EN + CN) support.
Use-case details: chat-first (support agent), fallback to embeddings for KB lookup and summarization of long tickets. Typical payloads: 600-1200 tokens per turn, average session 3-5 turns.
Targets: 95th pctl latency <300ms for single-turn chat (prefer ~200ms), sustained throughput ~40-60 req/min during peak, cold start caching desired.
Cost sensitivity: SMB budget — wants predictable < $0.10/request on average; willing to pay up to mid-range if quality reduces deflection to human agents.
Security: must be SOC2 compliant vendor, SSO/SAML for admin, audit logs retained 90 days. Data residency: primarily US, no strict EU residency requirement yet.
Model questions raised by engineering lead (quote): "Which variant gives best hallucination vs cost tradeoff for customer-facing answers? Can we run smaller model for routing + larger for long-form?"
Asked about quantized/ftx variants: interest in 4-bit/8-bit quantized Llama or Mistral to reduce token cost — wants Redwood guidance on latency impact and expected cost savings.

Multilingual note: 10% of customers interact in Mandarin; Qwen-14B mentioned as stronger in CN. Team asks if Redwood routing can send Chinese traffic to Qwen variant automatically while keeping English on cheaper Mistral/Llama config.
Ops concerns: SDK self-serve experience, api-key scoping, rate-limiting behavior during burst (they saw 429s in trial), and metrics for per-route cost breakdown.

Requested deliverables: 1) short model comparison table with expected token cost per 1k tokens and rough latency on hosted nodes; 2) sample eval run on 250 support prompts (they will provide dataset) showing answer quality + hallucination score; 3) example routing policy for language-aware model fallback.

Sales play: emphasize Redwood Optimize suggestions (auto-batching, prefix caching) to hit cost targets; demo per-route cost UI to finance during next call.
